_comment: STT backends for the audio lane of the segment-time benchmark. Three orthogonal axes per entry: (1) supported_hardware — explicit list of hardware-class keys from reference.json, or ['*'] for any class; the harness refuses to RTF-capture on a class outside this list. (2) fallback — production runtime behavior, 'use this if the preferred provider is unavailable'. (3) benchmarkable — whether the harness should run RTF capture; cloud backends are not benchmarkable in the RTF sense (network noise dominates) and use a flat wall_seconds_per_5min rule of thumb instead. parakeet (Solstone-internal CoreML / linux-x86_64 ONNX) and parakeet-nim (Spark NIM HTTP backend) are DISTINCT backends with different supported_hardware — do not unify them; that's the bug that triggered this split. RTF entries populated by `python -m think.benchmark.harness --transcriber <id> --audio-fixture <path> --class <hw>`.

parakeet.label: Parakeet TDT (Solstone-internal: CoreML / linux-x86_64 ONNX)
parakeet.notes: Bundled observe/transcribe/parakeet.py path: CoreML helper on macOS Apple Silicon, onnx-asr + onnxruntime on linux-x86_64. Does NOT run on linux/aarch64 (DGX Spark) — that platform uses parakeet-nim instead. The two are distinct backends; never collapse them.

parakeet-nim.label: Parakeet TDT (NVIDIA NIM container, HTTP)
parakeet-nim.requires: nvcr.io/nim/nvidia/parakeet-0-6b-tdt running and reachable at PARAKEET_NIM_URL (default http://localhost:9000). Harness hard-fails with 'NIM container not running at <url>' when unreachable; never silently falls back to another backend.
parakeet-nim.notes: Spark-specific deployment vector (Sortformer diarization + bundled Silero VAD). Provider implementation lands in Phase 3a alongside the NIM container deploy in the Cumulus stack; RTF measured in Phase 3b once the container is up.

whisper.label: Whisper (faster-whisper, local)
whisper.notes: Portable rollback only. Used in production when the preferred provider is unavailable. Whisper RTF is informative for the fallback path but should never be substituted for parakeet/parakeet-nim numbers in the headline benchmark — that would corrupt the cross-backend signal.

gemini.label: Gemini (cloud)
gemini.notes: Cloud backend with diarization. Wall-clock is network-bound; the flat wall_seconds_per_5min is a rule-of-thumb baseline, not a hardware-derived measurement. Not benchmarkable in the RTF sense.

revai.label: Rev.ai (cloud)
revai.notes: Cloud backend with diarization. Wall-clock includes provider-side queueing that varies by 2-3x; treat as a rough estimate. Not benchmarkable in the RTF sense.
